{
  "hook": "Valle de Tupungato's high-altitude vineyards at 1,300 meters push Atamisque Chardonnay toward green apple and citrus notes instead of tropical ripeness. Multiple vintages snag gold medals from Berliner and Asia Wine Trophies, signaling consistent quality. This wine delivers Mendoza's cool-climate edge at everyday prices.",
  "wine_summary": "Atamisque crafts this Chardonnay from Tupungato's elevated sites in Mendoza's Uco Valley, where the producer prioritizes small yields and precise farming to highlight varietal purity. The wines stand out for their balance, earning repeated gold medals across 2010, 2015, 2017, 2018, and NV vintages from international competitions. Terroir here—Andes foothills with diurnal temperature swings—locks in acidity while building subtle texture, making this a benchmark for high-altitude Argentine whites that punch above their weight.",
  "terroir_expression": "Alluvial soils mixed with calcareous deposits in Valle de Tupungato filter water efficiently, stressing vines to concentrate flavors into precise citrus and stone fruit. Nights drop to 10°C while days hit 25°C, preserving malic acid for bright green apple snap and mineral undertones from limestone bedrock. These elements translate to a wine with tension and length, dodging the flabby warmth of lower Mendoza sites.",
  "vinification_summary": "Partial oak fermentation and malolactic conversion—shifting sharp malic acid to creamy lactic—add restrained hazelnut layers without overwhelming fruit. Steel tank aging dominates to retain site-driven freshness, a choice that amplifies Tupungato's altitude effects over heavy wood influence. This approach yields wines with lift and subtle creaminess that age gracefully.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: acidity slices through spice while creamy notes soothe heat. Grilled octopus with romesco: mineral edge matches char and smoke, stone fruit echoes peppers. Lobster thermidor: buttery malolactic texture mirrors sauce richness without clashing acidity. Caesar salad: citrus punch amplifies dressing tang, green apple cuts creamy elements. Vietnamese pho: bright acid refreshes herbal broth, subtle oak tempers star anise warmth.",
  "comparable_wines": "Domaine Laroche Chablis Premier Cru—similar cool-climate citrus and mineral drive from Kimmeridgian soils. Felton Road Bannockburn Chardonnay—Central Otago's stony clays yield comparable tension and orchard fruit. Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc—Marlborough's high acidity and herbaceous lift mirror the style at a step up in price.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry white with vibrant acidity and subtle creamy texture",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2018 and younger now through 2028; store at 12-14°C away from light. Older vintages like 2010 hold firm structure for another 5 years.",
  "value_assessment": "$15-25 retail positions it against Catena Alta Chardonnay at $30 or O. Fournier Urban UC0 at $18. Gold medals across vintages confirm it overdelivers on freshness and balance. Buy multiples for the quality-to-price gap.",
  "market_position": "Casual drinkers grab this from supermarket shelves for weeknight versatility. Restaurant lists feature it in by-the-glass programs targeting value seekers. Sommeliers push it to tables pairing with seafood or poultry.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you demand overt oak bombast—this prioritizes site transparency over cellar drama. Most chase buttery California styles and miss how Tupungato's altitude crafts superior food wines. Stock it if lean, tense whites spark your interest.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 1,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 8,

  }
}

Multiple vintages snag gold medals from Berliner and Asia Wine Trophies, signaling consistent quality. This wine delivers Mendoza's cool-climate edge at everyday prices.
parsed.wine_summary: Atamisque crafts this Chardonnay from Tupungato's elevated sites in Mendoza's Uco Valley, where the producer prioritizes small yields and precise farming to highlight varietal purity. The wines stand out for their balance, earning repeated gold medals across 2010, 2015, 2017, 2018, and NV vintages from international competitions. Terroir here—Andes foothills with diurnal temperature swings—locks in acidity while building subtle texture, making this a benchmark for high-altitude Argentine whites that punch above their weight.
parsed.terroir_expression: Alluvial soils mixed with calcareous deposits in Valle de Tupungato filter water efficiently, stressing vines to concentrate flavors into precise citrus and stone fruit. Nights drop to 10°C while days hit 25°C, preserving malic acid for bright green apple snap and mineral undertones from limestone bedrock. These elements translate to a wine with tension and length, dodging the flabby warmth of lower Mendoza sites.
parsed.vinification_summary: Partial oak fermentation and malolactic conversion—shifting sharp malic acid to creamy lactic—add restrained hazelnut layers without overwhelming fruit. Steel tank aging dominates to retain site-driven freshness, a choice that amplifies Tupungato's altitude effects over heavy wood influence. This approach yields wines with lift and subtle creaminess that age gracefully.
